title: Subsets II
prompt:
Given an array that **may contain duplicates**, return all unique subsets (no duplicate subsets in the output).

**Example**: `[1,2,2]` → `[[],[1],[1,2],[1,2,2],[2],[2,2]]`.

Sort first, then skip a duplicate value when it would start a sibling branch identical to one already explored.
hints: Record a copy of the path at every node (like plain Subsets).
In the loop, `if (i > start && nums[i] == nums[i-1]) continue;` — skip duplicate values at the same recursion depth.

solution.explanation: The `i > start` guard only skips duplicates that would begin a *sibling* branch (same depth) — the first occurrence still recurses, so `[2,2]` is reachable while a second identical `[2]`-first branch is pruned. Sorting is what makes duplicates adjacent and this test valid.
